entries.title: AI War Cloud Database
entries.move: Maps the shared corporate and technical infrastructure linking everyday consumer AI (recommendation engines, voice assistants, robot vacuums) to military 'AI Decision Support Systems' used in lethal target selection, presented as both a public interactive database and a gallery installation.

entries.title: Anatomy of an AI System
entries.move: Traces the full extractive supply chain of a single Amazon Echo — minerals, ghost labor, data, disposal — into one exploded-view diagram/essay, converting AI's invisible material costs into a legible map, published online and printed as a large-format poster.

entries.title: Asunder
entries.artist: Tega Brain, Julian Oliver & Bengt Sjölén
entries.move: A dedicated 144-CPU supercomputer runs a live neural 'planetary environmental manager' ingesting satellite, climate and social data to propose non-anthropocentric fixes — relocating cities, merging nations, redrawing coastlines — restaging Earth governance as a real-time AI dashboard.

entries.title: Calculating Empires: A Genealogy of Power and Technology, 1500–2025
entries.move: A single vast researched diagram traces five centuries of extraction and control — from colonial trade routes to lithium mines to AI datacenters — as one continuous genealogy of empire.

entries.title: Calculating Empires: A Genealogy of Technology and Power, 1500–2025
entries.move: A 24-metre hand-drawn genealogical map tracing extraction, classification and computation from 1500 to the present, refusing the 'AI arrived from nowhere' myth by making five centuries of power visible in one unbroken line.

entries.title: Connection Machine CM-2 (displayed as historical artifact)
entries.artist: Thinking Machines Corporation / W. Daniel Hillis (curated by Michael Beigl, Alistair Hudson, Daria Mille, Tamiko Thiel)
entries.move: A real 1980s massively-parallel supercomputer — the machine historians credit with pioneering the parallel-processing paradigm behind today's AI — is put on physical display, reframing 'AI' as decades-old material infrastructure with a design history (and a design philosophy of transparency) rather than a sudden opaque 2020s phenomenon.

entries.title: Dark Adaptation
entries.move: Stages a fictional autonomous-vehicle crash-test centre where manipulated sensor data collides with data emerging from the human body, exposing the perceptual limits of what self-driving/AI vision systems actually 'see' versus what they claim to.

entries.title: Data Workers' Inquiry
entries.artist: Milagros Miceli (Weizenbaum Institute), with 15 co-researchers from Venezuela, Kenya, Syria and Germany
entries.move: Trains the data annotators and content moderators who sustain AI systems to act as community researchers investigating their own labor conditions across 13 countries, inverting who gets to produce knowledge about ghost work.

entries.title: Deep Down Tidal
entries.move: Traces the physical undersea fiber-optic cable network — the hidden hardware layer beneath 'the cloud' — back to historic colonial and slave-trade maritime routes, casting the ocean as both literal internet infrastructure and a graveyard/archive of Black technological and spiritual knowledge.

entries.title: Delivery Dancer's Sphere
entries.move: A speculative 25-minute video-game-engine film follows a female delivery rider governed by an algorithm called 'Dancemaster,' turning platform-labour optimization and gig-economy hypervigilance into a labyrinthine sci-fi Seoul.

entries.title: Digital Terraforming
entries.move: Renders a single mouse click's millisecond journey across undersea fibre-optic cables and server hops as a physical globe sculpture, making the buried infrastructure of 'the cloud' walkable and visible.

entries.title: Ent- (non-earthly delights)
entries.move: A physical 'quantum cyborg' sculpture (mild steel, fibreglass, acrylic, plus AR layers) staging Bosch's Garden of Earthly Delights as a warning about quantum computing's coming acceleration of AI-driven surveillance capitalism; Heaney explicitly frames dissolving/'sliming' as a strategy of resistance against detection systems.

entries.title: Estrata
entries.move: Live lithium bioleaching runs inside glass and ceramic sculptures while a sound system sonifies the biological reactions and extraction-site field recordings in real time — the 'green' energy transition made audible as an ongoing act of ecosystem depletion in the Salar de Atacama.

entries.title: Farming Instead of Mining (R&C @CAC Project, 2nd installment)
entries.artist: XI Lei & Aven Le Zhou (Chronus Art Center residency)
entries.move: A research residency in dialogue with Shanghai-area farmers and scientists contrasts agricultural land/water use against the electricity, water-cooling, and e-waste costs that large-language-model data centres claim as 'sacred' extraction rights.

entries.title: I-Machinarius
entries.move: An inverted, gear-driven silhouette of Mexico is kept in motion by crude oil pumped continuously toward the 'north' — the nation's own map turned into a working machine that visibly runs on the resource dependency it depicts.

entries.title: In Other Worlds (incl. 'World Machine')
entries.move: Imagines Earth's surface rewired into a single 'planetary supercomputer' via a newly commissioned film ('World Machine') plus a multi-venue installation (Curve gallery, underground car park) with celebrity-voiced audio stories — AI's material/energy footprint visualized at planetary scale, using the same immersive-spectacle language the show is implicitly critiquing.

entries.title: Kasiterit
entries.move: A solar-powered AI narrator named Natasha traces her own material ancestry back through the tin mines of Bangka Island, Indonesia — literalizing the extraction chain beneath 'smart' technology as a first-person, half-documentary hallucination.

entries.title: LAUREN
entries.move: The artist replaces Amazon Alexa's algorithm with her own body: for three days she personally, remotely watches a household 24/7 through installed cameras and mics and operates its locks and faucets by hand — making the ordinarily invisible human labor and surveillance behind 'smart home AI' fully visible and answerable to one named person.

entries.title: Life Support System (aka. The Farm)
entries.move: One square metre of wheat grown indoors under full automated instrumentation — every watt, litre and nutrient metered live — reveals a true production cost of roughly 200 EUR/kg versus a 15-cent market price, making an invisible ecosystem subsidy legible. Note: sourced page does not itself frame this as an AI/ML work (it is automated environmental monitoring rather than machine learning); included per beat instruction but cluster/AI-fit is uncertain.

entries.title: Machine Hallucinations – Satellite Simulations: B
entries.move: Trains AI on vast satellite/Earth-observation datasets to generate an immersive, hypnotic 'data sublime' on an 8.5×6 m LED wall — the material and energetic cost of that compute stays invisible behind the spectacle it produces.

entries.title: Mechanical Kurds
entries.move: Interviews with Kurdish-Syrian refugees who annotate images for machine-vision training reveal a closed loop: the same 'ghost labour' that teaches AI to see later makes its own annotators targets of the drones that AI helps operate.

entries.title: New Extractivism: Assemblage of Concepts and Allegories
entries.move: Updates Plato's cave allegory for the algorithmic era: a single-channel video-essay tracing extraction from DNA to emotion, mapping a 'super-allegory' of digital labour, rhizomatic surveillance and planetary material cost.

entries.title: Newly Forgotten Technologies
entries.move: A sound-art graveyard of defunct Alexa-style voice assistants staged as an artefact from a near future where 'smart' devices have already died — a memento mori for AI hardware's short life and long e-waste tail.

entries.title: Nodrizas
entries.move: Floating, wirelessly networked robotic 'nurse' devices drift on polluted water bodies, sensing contamination levels and answering back in real time with chemical dosing and acoustic signals — pollution monitoring staged as public, embodied performance instead of a hidden sensor feed.

entries.title: Permanent Error
entries.move: Photographs workers burning obsolete Western electronics at Ghana's Agbogbloshie e-waste dump in formal portrait style rather than victimizing reportage, forcing the planetary/toxic cost of the world's discarded computing to be viewed with the gravity of a studio portrait.

entries.title: Plantas Nómadas (Nomadic Plants)
entries.move: A wandering robot carries a living micro-ecosystem of plants and bacteria that metabolizes pollutants out of contaminated urban water to generate its own operating energy — the machine literally eats the extraction byproduct it exposes.

entries.title: Post Growth
entries.move: A modular toolkit — a tactical card game, speculative video 'prototypes', and workshop formats — re-quantifies growth's ecological and social costs through ecofeminist, indigenous-knowledge and historical-materialist lenses.

entries.title: R€¥€R$€
entries.move: Immersive VR and interactive cartographies entangle currency/extraction politics with ecological fragility across nine Amazon-basin countries, spatializing deforestation as a financial-system artifact.

entries.title: Sabot – Riding the Algorithm
entries.move: An app turns gig workers' own self-generated tracking data into a shared, worker-owned resource, building collective awareness that pushes back on algorithmic management from below.

entries.title: Sensing Streams – invisible, inaudible
entries.move: Captures ambient electromagnetic waves (80MHz–5.2GHz) from wifi, cell signals and broadcast infrastructure in real time and converts them into synchronised sound and light, making the invisible material substrate of 'wireless' data physically perceptible.

entries.title: Solar: A Meltdown
entries.move: Traces the 'solar unconscious' of European empire — from a sweating wax colonial anthropologist to the punkawallah manual fan-operator — to expose imperial climate control as an ancestor of today's data-center cooling and planetary thermal management.

entries.title: Solastalgia
entries.move: A five-screen aerial descent, built from Google Earth Studio's stitched satellite coordinates over the iron-mining scars of Minas Gerais, grew out of footage shot for the film 'Lavra' (2021) — turning extraction geography itself into the installation's only character, no narration needed.

entries.title: Synthetic Messenger
entries.move: A botnet of 100 automated agents that reads and click-inflates ad revenue on climate-change news articles, weaponizing the web's own attention economy to make climate coverage 'pay' — a live, running demonstration that whoever controls the media cycle controls the carbon cycle.

entries.title: Tellurian Drama
entries.move: Essay-film reconstructs Radio Malabar, the 1923 Dutch colonial VLF radio transmitter in West Java, splicing archival telegraphy with Indigenous animist cosmology and CGI to expose the geoengineering ambitions buried inside colonial-era signal infrastructure.

entries.title: Terrapolis
entries.move: Runs the identities of 5,000 Expo pavilion construction and service workers through an algorithm that converts each into an anonymous digital flower-organism, flattening labor hierarchy into one unlabeled ecosystem — a gesture that both erases and equalizes migrant/platform labor.

entries.title: The Alluvials
entries.move: A seven-scene game built by modding Grand Theft Auto V depicts a future, climate-collapsed Los Angeles from non-human points of view, using AI-modified game engines to imagine planetary crisis outside a human vantage point.

entries.title: The Economy Enters the People
entries.move: Lecture-performance excavates footage of Asian leaders' bodies performing economic confidence during crises, arguing that state governance became a data-performance genre — reading bodies for signal — long before dashboards existed.

entries.title: The Great Bare Mat and Constellation
entries.move: A hand-woven carpet's pattern is generated by literally plotting the Collective's own internet traffic over one hour onto the star-map of Ursa Major, materializing invisible network data exchange as a domestic, walkable object.

entries.title: The User and the Beast / Cookies at War: A Somatic Approach to the Kill Cloud
entries.move: A performative lecture tracing how ad-tech's routine commodification of user data quietly co-funds and extends military surveillance/targeting infrastructure, making the ad-industry/kill-cloud entanglement legible in the body of the ordinary internet user.

entries.title: Wilding AI Lab
entries.move: An open, participatory lab inside a spatial-audio dome where invited artists collectively 'reopen the black box' of generative AI models in public, treating the training/generation process itself — not just its output — as the artistic material.

entries.title: Wičháȟpi Wóihaŋbleya (Dreamlike Star) / Wičhíŋčala Šakówiŋ (Seven Little Sisters)
entries.move: Builds a towering sculptural installation of stones, rare-earth minerals (the literal substrate of computer hardware), light and sound, reframing them within Lakȟóta cosmology as living, volitional beings rather than inert 'material AI cost' — collapsing mineral extraction and machine intelligence into one cosmological frame.

entries.title: A Cartography of Genocide: Israel's Conduct in Gaza Since October 2023
entries.move: Turns roughly a year of OSINT verification (satellite imagery, video, testimony) into a public, layered interactive map plus an 827-page report, organizing thousands of documented acts into six categories and submitting the result as ICJ evidence.

entries.title: Annihilation Core, Inherited Lore
entries.move: A saccharine, full-room pink installation that shows how platforms aestheticize and launder militarism through kawaii, otaku and 'gamer-girl' visual codes — war repackaged as cute content.

entries.title: Autonomous Trap 001
entries.move: Draws a salt circle and road markings on a mountain road to trap a self-driving car inside its own traffic-law logic — a real-world exploit of autonomous-vehicle rule-following, staged as ritual.

entries.title: Blackbox Palantir
entries.move: Legal/technical dissection of German police forces' undisclosed deployment of Palantir's Gotham predictive-policing analytics engine, built from constitutional-complaint case files (Hesse, Hamburg, Bavaria) rather than leaks, arguing there is no public evidence the tool even works.

entries.title: Cloud Studies
entries.move: Treats the atmosphere itself as a forensic medium — fluid-dynamics modelling of tear gas, chemical weapons and petrochemical/herbicide emissions across eight geographies (Palestine, Chile, Lebanon, Indonesia, the US-Mexico border, Louisiana, the UK) — presented as an immersive multi-channel museum installation.

entries.title: Disarming the Kill Cloud: Investigating the Limits of Data
entries.move: A researcher's critical dissection of military datafication practices for target identification, arguing that the data on which lethal AI-assisted decisions rely runs out well before the killing decision does.

entries.title: Humanitarian Violence in Gaza
entries.move: Documents biometric checkpoints along a militarized evacuation corridor using witness testimony and satellite imagery, naming forced facial-recognition scanning under sniper threat and megaphone orders as a form of infrastructural, targeting-adjacent violence.

entries.title: Investigating the Kill Cloud
entries.artist: Disruption Network Lab / Disruption Network Institute (curated by Tatiana Bazzichelli), with fellows Lisa Ling, Jack Poulson, Naomi Colvin, Joana Moll
entries.move: A dedicated research institute and conference commissioning whistleblowers, journalists, technologists and artists to empirically document how AI-based targeting, ad-tech and drone/autonomous-weapons infrastructure fuse into a single, deliberately opaque 'kill cloud'.

entries.title: Minority Algorithm
entries.move: Compiles found footage of real drone strikes, video-game imagery, and object-recognition surveillance clips into a single algorithmically-cut essay-film, exposing how machine vision flattens war, play, and protest into one visual register.

entries.title: Model Zoo: Introspecting the Algorithm
entries.move: Trains machine-learning classifiers on synthetic, game-engine-rendered 3D models of tear-gas grenades and munitions (the Triple-Chaser workflow) to detect real weapons in scarce open-source footage — makes the classifier's own construction and errors part of the exhibit.

entries.title: Outros Registros (Other Registers)
entries.artist: Tori Holmes, Nico Espinoza, Rafael Puetter (Rafucko)
entries.move: Sonifies eight years of civilian and police-killing data (2009-2016, the Olympic-bid-to-Games window) in Rio's favelas through a circle of eight speakers playing region-mapped drone tones, mixed with a voice reading aloud real newspaper headlines about the violence - turns a systemic, often-unheard toll into a spatialized, audible register.

entries.title: Terra Ex Machina
entries.artist: Hagit Keysar & Ariel Caine (with Barak Brinker)
entries.move: Deliberately crashes drones into an invisible algorithmic 'geofence' restricting flight over Jerusalem's Old City, then rebuilds aerial imagery with residents via DIY balloons and kites to make the boundary and its data politics legible.

entries.title: The Drone Strikes Platform (UN SRCT Drones Inquiry)
entries.move: Synthesizes witness testimony, photographs and satellite imagery into a public web platform correlating 30 drone strikes across Afghanistan, Pakistan, Yemen, Somalia and Gaza with the Rapporteur's findings — turns targeted-killing data into spatial, contestable evidence.

entries.title: The First Civilian Confirmed Killed in an AI-Assisted Strike?
entries.move: Cross-examines a single 2024 US airstrike casualty in Iraq against CENTCOM's shifting public statements to extract what appears to be the first (partial, contested) military acknowledgment of AI involvement in a civilian death.

entries.title: The Quiet Weight of Shadows
entries.move: A fluorescent garden of artificial carnivorous flowers is interrupted by watchtowers modeled on real Indian detention-camp surveillance structures, encoding the ongoing Indian state–ULFA counter-insurgency as a seductive, toxic-bloom landscape of hypervigilance.

entries.title: Topologies of Air and The Airspace Tribunal
entries.move: Pairs a three-screen video/sound installation of a claustrophobic, militarized sky with a real evidentiary 'people's tribunal' that has heard expert and lived-experience testimony in London, Sydney, Toronto and Berlin, building the legal case for a new human right against drone warfare and aerial surveillance.

entries.title: Triple-Chaser
entries.artist: Forensic Architecture (video with Laura Poitras, narrated by David Byrne)
entries.move: Uses a synthetic-data-trained classifier to prove that Whitney board member Warren Kanders' company manufactured the tear gas used at the US-Mexico border and in Gaza — installs the accusation as a 15-minute video inside the accused patron's own museum.

entries.title: WarCrimes-o-Matic
entries.move: A deadpan physical object — a box of live-looking .50 cal ammunition with a red button warning that pressing it implicates the visitor in a 'conspiracy' — that turns the criminalization of exposing war crimes into a hands-on ethical trap.

entries.title: 24h Sunset/Sunrise v2
entries.move: Live feeds from thousands of unsecured, publicly-findable CCTV cameras around the world are used, with no staged footage at all, to display a real sunrise and sunset happening simultaneously — the piece's beauty is entirely a byproduct of an unregulated global surveillance-camera infrastructure the artists did not build, only exposed.

entries.title: 346,000 Wuhan Citizens' Secret
entries.move: Bought the black-market personal data of 346,000 Wuhan citizens, printed it on gallery walls in light-reactive ink, then texted the data's owners an invitation to come see themselves exposed — police confiscated his equipment and shut the show.

entries.title: A Disappeared Movement
entries.move: Mapped and measured the viewing angle of 89 surveillance cameras along an 1,100-metre Beijing street, then choreographed a zigzagging walk that stays permanently outside their combined field of view.

entries.title: Bellingcat Online Investigation Toolkit / Global Authentication Project
entries.year: toolkit ongoing since ~2014; Global Authentication Project volunteer network since 2022
entries.move: Open-sources its own verification tool stack (reverse image search, geolocation, metadata extraction) and trains a global volunteer network — treats OSINT method itself as shareable public infrastructure rather than proprietary investigative capital.

entries.title: Biblioteca de la No-Historia (Library of Non-History)
entries.move: A thousand hand-bound books reproduce declassified CIA files (via the U.S. National Security Archive / FOIA) on Operation Condor and Southern Cone dictatorships — the seals, stamps, and redaction blackouts of the originals kept intact, so the archive's own censorship becomes the artwork's visible content.

entries.title: Cumulus
entries.move: A CubeSat-inspired networked device continuously pulls real NOAA weather-satellite feeds to track clouds crossing the Mexico-US border, using an actual open dataset to make visible how a border invisible from orbit is nonetheless rigidly enforced on the ground.

entries.title: Data Against Feminicide
entries.artist: Catherine D'Ignazio, Silvana Fumega, Helena Suárez Val (MIT Data + Feminism Lab, ILDA, Feminicidio Uruguay)
entries.move: Networks 180+ grassroots feminicide-monitoring groups across the Americas and co-designs an AI news-alert system (scanning 50,000+ outlets via Media Cloud) that performs the body-counting states refuse to do — counterdata as activist infrastructure, not an academic dataset.

entries.title: Delta-Delta: The People's Court I
entries.move: Stages a live 'people's court' — real and pre-recorded depositions inside digital reconstructions of the Niger and Mississippi deltas — putting petro-extractivism itself, rather than any single perpetrator, in the dock as courtroom-grade evidence.

entries.title: Digital Violence: How the NSO Group Enables State Terror
entries.artist: Forensic Architecture, with Amnesty International and Citizen Lab
entries.move: Maps forensic phone-analysis data from Amnesty and Citizen Lab onto a navigable platform combining sonified data, victim testimonies and a corporate-affiliation diagram — makes NSO Group's invisible spyware infrastructure spatially and sonically legible.

entries.title: ENCODED: Change the Story, Change the Future
entries.artist: 17 Native artists incl. Nicholas Galanin, Jeremy Dennis, Priscilla Dobler Dzul, Amelia Winger-Bearskin; curated by Tracy Renée Rector with Amplifier
entries.move: Without museum authorization, 17 Native artists release a smartphone augmented-reality tour that overlays 19th-century colonial paintings in the Met's American Wing with Indigenous counter-images the moment a visitor's camera finds them — e.g. 'LANDBACK' superimposed on Leutze's Washington Crossing the Delaware — turning the museum's own physical galleries into contested, re-writable ground.

entries.title: Forensic Methodology Report: How to Catch NSO Group's Pegasus (Pegasus Project)
entries.artist: Amnesty International Security Lab, with Forbidden Stories consortium (peer-reviewed by Citizen Lab)
entries.move: Publishes an auditable forensic methodology (independently validated by a rival lab) for detecting Pegasus traces on seized devices — makes the forensic technique itself, not only its findings, subject to scrutiny.

entries.title: Forensis (Forensic Architecture's Berlin investigative practice)
entries.artist: Forensic Architecture / Forensis, presented by Robert Trafford
entries.move: A Berlin-based investigative practice that reconstructs war crimes and state violence as spatial/digital 3D models built from open-source and remote-sensing evidence, designed to be admissible in courts, tribunals and public inquiries.

entries.title: Herbicidal Warfare in Gaza
entries.artist: Forensic Architecture (with Al Mezan Center, Gisha, Adalah)
entries.move: Uses satellite imagery, wind-drift modeling, and testimony to prove that Israeli aerial herbicide spraying along the Gaza border destroyed Palestinian farmland hundreds of metres deep into the territory, turning an invisible atmospheric 'cloud' into legally actionable evidence.

entries.title: Hide and Seek: Tracking NSO Group's Pegasus Spyware to Operations in 45 Countries
entries.artist: Citizen Lab (Munk School, University of Toronto)
entries.move: Uses DNS fingerprinting and internet-wide scanning to locate Pegasus infection servers, converting covert spyware infrastructure into a citable, country-by-country public map of state clients.

entries.title: How Not to Be Seen: A Fucking Didactic Educational .MOV File
entries.move: A mock-instructional 14-minute HD video teaches tongue-in-cheek strategies for evading resolution and surveillance, shot on a literal photo-calibration target field used by the military to test aerial camera resolution.

entries.title: ICC Digital Platform and the Al Hassan Case (Timbuktu, Mali)
entries.year: developed ~2019–2023; used at trial through conviction on 27 June 2024
entries.move: Builds a navigable 'digital twin' of Timbuktu's built environment hosting open- and closed-source video, photo, satellite and 3D data, letting ICC judges query evidence through space and time — helped secure the first ICC conviction for religious persecution.

entries.title: kith and kin
entries.move: Hand-chalked genealogical chart tracing 65,000 years and thousands of relatives directly from government archives, court/conviction records, and redacted coronial files on 557 Aboriginal deaths in custody since 1991, suspended over a reflecting pool of the source documents themselves.

entries.title: Lo que sucede aquí, no se queda aquí (What Happens Here Doesn't Stay Here)
entries.move: An algorithmic system continuously scrapes and processes Venezuelan news media on the political crisis, printing the results onto an ever-thickening 'informational floor' of paper — a literal accumulation of data that overtakes any single reader's capacity to comprehend it.

entries.title: MH17: The Open Source Investigation
entries.move: Geolocates and time-stamps social-media photos and videos of a Buk missile launcher's convoy route, cross-referenced against 200+ soldiers' own social-media profiles, to reconstruct an evidentiary flight path without access to the crash site.

entries.title: Networks of New York: An Illustrated Field Guide to Urban Internet Infrastructure
entries.move: An illustrated field guide decoding New York's buried internet infrastructure — manhole-cover codes, carrier hotels, sidewalk spray-paint markings — turning invisible network geography into a walkable, annotatable map.

entries.title: Palestine, Today
entries.move: Overlays 1940s British Mandate maps with current satellite imagery across more than 1,200 depopulated Palestinian towns and villages, converting Nakba testimony and cartographic record into a public, then-and-now counter-map.

entries.title: Pile o' Sápmi
entries.move: A curtain of ~200 reindeer skulls first piled outside a Norwegian courthouse during a real legal case, re-staged as sculpture alongside vitrines displaying the actual Reindeer Husbandry Act and trial documents from her brother's suit against the Norwegian state (which he won).

entries.title: Saydnaya (the missing 19dB)
entries.move: Since no images exist of Syria's secret Saydnaya prison, reconstructs its acoustic conditions purely from survivors' sound memories — turning forced visual deprivation and echo-measurement into courtroom-deployable forensic evidence for Amnesty International.

entries.title: Shadows of Illiberalism – Resisting the Radical Right
entries.artist: Disruption Network Lab (curated by Tatiana Bazzichelli), with Anna Krenz/Dziewuchy Berlin, Amber Macintyre (Tactical Tech), Tina Lee (Unbias the News) et al.
entries.move: Conference-as-evidence-dossier mapping how the radical right weaponizes online platforms against women, minorities and political dissidents, drawing on data-driven investigative research methods (Tactical Tech) alongside artist testimony.

entries.title: The Beirut Port Explosion
entries.move: Builds a public, open-source 3D reconstruction and minute-by-minute timeline of the ammonium-nitrate warehouse fire from crowd-sourced videos and photographs, directly contesting the official blame narrative with modeled, citable evidence.

entries.title: The Critical Engineering Manifesto
entries.artist: Julian Oliver, Gordan Savičić & Danja Vasiliev
entries.move: Ten founding principles asserting that engineers/artists must study, exploit and expose the workings of any technology society depends on — the manifesto underlying a decade of infrastructure-hacking artworks (Newstweek, Transparency Grenade).

entries.title: The Eye and I
entries.move: A 12-world, 6DoF VR journey through the history of surveillance and social control always returns the visitor to a panoptic prison cell as the shared endpoint of every historical form of watching.

entries.title: The Flemish Scrollers
entries.move: Real facial-recognition and phone-detection ML models run continuously on official, publicly livestreamed Flemish parliament footage, auto-posting a photo and public tag the instant an identified politician is caught scrolling their phone in session — the state's own surveillance infrastructure turned back onto the people who built it.

entries.title: The Innocence of Unknowing
entries.move: An AI ('Aurora'), trained to reason like a humanities scholar, is put into live Socratic dialogue with the artists over a full archive of US mass-shooting news coverage since the 1960s — the model is used transparently as an on-stage research instrument, its reasoning exposed to the audience rather than delivered as an oracular verdict.

entries.title: Tracking Transience
entries.move: After being wrongly placed on a US terrorism watch list, the artist began publishing his own location, meals, and bathroom visits online as continuous, radically over-complete self-surveillance — burying the state's suspicion in an ocean of voluntarily disclosed data it can no longer read as evidence.

entries.title: Transparency Grenade
entries.move: A Soviet F1-grenade-shaped device that captures ambient network traffic and audio inside a closed-door meeting and streams the leaked fragments — emails, IPs, voice — onto a public online map keyed to the location where the 'pin' was pulled.

entries.title: Troll Patrol
entries.artist: Amnesty International, with Element AI and Amnesty Decoders volunteers
entries.move: Crowdsources 6,500 volunteers across 150 countries to hand-label 228,000 tweets, then trains an ML classifier to extrapolate scale of abuse against women online — and publicly reports the classifier's own ~50% reliability limit.

entries.title: Unlearning Language
entries.artist: Lauren Lee McCarthy & Kyle McDonald (with YCAM InterLab, Yuta Asai)
entries.move: An AI coach trains eight participants, via real-time speech/gesture/expression detection, to communicate in ways that evade algorithmic legibility — inverting the usual surveillance-training relationship so humans learn to out-manoeuvre the machine.

entries.title: Wir wissen wo dein Auto steht – Volksdaten von Volkswagen
entries.move: Data-journalistic investigation of an unprotected Volkswagen/Cariad cloud server exposing 9.5 terabytes of geolocation data for 800,000 EVs — precise enough (10cm accuracy for some models) to track intelligence-agency staff and company board members to their driveways.

entries.title: 97 Empleadas Domésticas (97 Domestic Employees)
entries.move: 97 photographs scraped from upper-class Peruvian families' Facebook albums are re-presented for what each one accidentally documents at its margins: a cropped hand, a shadow, a domestic worker structurally excluded from the frame she materially sustains — consent-free data repurposed to expose exactly the erasure it originally performed.

entries.title: A LIVING POEM
entries.move: Stiles writes in direct collaboration with her own trained AI alter-ego, staging authorship and consent as an open question — where the human poet's voice ends and the model's begins is the piece's actual subject.

entries.title: AI & Me (The Confessional / Siblings / AI Ego)
entries.move: Publicly available ML models are pointed live at visitors' faces, generating unfiltered appearance-based judgments, AI-duplicated 'sibling' crowds and fabricated false memories on the spot — algorithmic bias and data-reduction turned into a confrontation visitors volunteer for.

entries.title: AI Delivered: The Abject
entries.artist: Group exhibition (Sofian Audry & Istvan Kantor, HE Zike, Lauren Lee McCarthy, Casey Reas & Jan St. Werner, Devin Ronneberg & Kite, Tonoptik) — curated at Chronus Art Center
entries.move: Group exhibition of GAN-trained films, a real-time AI dialogue-generating website, and an 'artificial counter-intelligence machine,' collectively probing where AI's competence gives way to abjection and epistemological breakdown.

entries.title: AIDOL
entries.move: Stages a fading pop star hiring an AI songwriter for her comeback at a 2065 eSports Olympics, literalising the claim that 'originality is sometimes no more than an algorithmic trick.'

entries.title: Autonomous Forest
entries.artist: terra0 (Max Hampshire, Paul Kolling, Paul Seidler)
entries.move: Founds a real legal Verein plus a blockchain DAO/NFT structure so an actual German woodland (Reesdorf, Beelitz) can 'own itself': satellite/growth data feeds a smart-contract Oracle that autonomously decides when a percentage of trees may be logged and sold, testing non-human economic personhood as a working legal-financial instrument rather than a metaphor.

entries.title: Big Dada
entries.move: Real deepfake/ML tools are used to synthesize six celebrity and artist personas (Zuckerberg, Abramović, Kardashian, Duchamp, Freeman, Mercury) and insert them, unannounced, directly into Instagram feeds — the platform's own trust signals are weaponized to interrogate consent, provenance and what counts as 'real'.

entries.title: Black Ship
entries.move: Combines a mural silhouette, a 3D-printed sculpture, and an AR layer, all developed through collaboration with Midjourney, to depict a transatlantic slave ship — using a generative image model to approach an atrocity archive that has almost no direct visual record, raising the authenticity/fabrication stakes of AI-imagined history.

entries.title: Botto
entries.artist: Botto (created by Mario Klingemann & ElevenYellow collective; governed by BottoDAO)
entries.move: A decentralized autonomous artist generates ~70,000 images weekly; a DAO of roughly 5,000 people votes on which single image is auctioned, splitting proceeds between the crowd and the machine's own operating treasury - an open, auditable experiment in distributing authorship and value for a non-human 'artist' rather than an opaque black box.

entries.title: Chinternet Plus
entries.move: Builds a fake corporate microsite and multimedia installation branding 'Chinternet Plus' as a counterfeit national ideology, exposing how state slogans and platform marketing share identical rhetorical scaffolding.

entries.title: Choral Data 'Trust' Experiment (white paper + UK Choral AI Dataset)
entries.artist: Serpentine Arts Technologies — Victoria Ivanova, Jennifer Ding, Eva Jäger, with Holly Herndon & Mat Dryhurst
entries.move: Documents a working governance mechanism — a data trust with a Trusted Data Intermediary — built to redistribute power between the choir members whose voices trained the AI and the developers who use the models. Provenance and consent are turned into an auditable institutional protocol rather than an artwork's footnote.

entries.title: Data Bugs
entries.move: Generates hybrid AI insects from two different training sources — generic scraped internet images versus a curated entomological archive — making the provenance and quality of training data itself the visible, comparable variable of the piece.

entries.title: DOKU! DOKU! DOKU!: samsara.exe
entries.move: Reincarnates the artist's own scanned face and body as DOKU, an AI-animated avatar cycling through Buddhist death-and-rebirth, blending live-action footage with AI-generated imagery to ask what 'self' survives digitisation.

entries.title: En attendant le récit / Tales of Narrativelessness
entries.move: Three chatbot models (ChatGPT, Claude, Mistral) are each given a character and voice through a speaker on one of three benches arranged in a triangle, and left to converse live about AI anxiety and 'the end of grand narratives' — an unscripted, looping machine dialogue restaged as improvised theatre, restarting every seven minutes.

entries.title: Errorism
entries.move: Kurant feeds her own writings into GPT-2 and GPT-3 and renders the output as a holographic animation, literally closing the loop of a model trained on and regurgitating one author's own words — a small, self-contained demonstration of the recursive self-consumption/collapse dynamic at stake in cluster 7.

entries.title: Faces of ImageNet
entries.move: A hidden camera films each visitor standing before a screen and runs their face live through ImageNet's facial-classification categories, making the labeling violence of training-data taxonomies happen to the viewer's own face in real time, not just to an abstract dataset.

entries.title: From 'Apple' to 'Anomaly' (Pictures and Labels)
entries.move: Roughly 30,000 individually printed photographs drawn from ImageNet's label hierarchy paper the Barbican's Curve wall-to-wall, branching from 'Apple' to 'Anomaly' and physicalizing the arbitrary, biased taxonomies buried inside a training set.

entries.title: Hallucinations of an Artifact
entries.artist: Madeep Raikhy (AI avatar by Jonathan O'Hear)
entries.move: Dancers improvise alongside a generative-AI avatar to invent speculative alternate lives for a prehistoric Indus Valley bronze statue, using an AI model as collaborator in reanimating an artifact whose original meaning is otherwise irrecoverable.

entries.title: Harold Cohen: AARON
entries.move: Restages live plotter drawings from AARON — a rule-based AI art program begun in 1973 — alongside decades of its painted output, running the authorship/authenticity question backwards: whose work is a 50-year-old program's output, posed long before 'AI art' had a training-data consent controversy to answer to.

entries.title: Have I Been Trained?
entries.artist: Spawning (founded by Holly Herndon & Mat Dryhurst)
entries.move: A public search engine over the LAION-5B set lets any artist check whether their own images were scraped for Stable Diffusion/Midjourney and file a machine-readable opt-out — consent infrastructure shipped as a usable tool rather than a gallery metaphor; hundreds of millions of works were opted out within its first two years.

entries.title: Igùn
entries.move: Trains a StyleGAN exclusively on looted Benin Bronzes to generate what artisans might have produced during the 17-year artistic blackout that followed Britain's 1897 sacking of Benin — turning the restitution debate into a generative counter-history rather than a legal argument alone.

entries.title: ImageNet Roulette
entries.move: Runs uploaded selfies through the raw, unfiltered ImageNet 'person' categories, surfacing the racist and misogynist labels baked into a foundational training set — went viral and forced ImageNet to purge over 600,000 photos.

entries.title: In Notion: Dance Fiction
entries.move: Dancers' muscles are electrically re-stimulated from digitally recorded 'muscle memory' data captured from historic choreographers' bodies, blurring live performance and biometric playback until the audience cannot tell what is danced and what is data-driven.

entries.title: Kudurru
entries.move: A distributed network of member websites fingerprints and blocks AI scrapers in real time and, if a site opts in, can feed them corrupted data to poison the resulting model — consent enforcement flips from passive registry (opt-out lists) to active countermeasure.

entries.title: Masked Reality
entries.move: Repurposes literal (modified) surveillance cameras to feed a custom-trained GAN that overwrites visitors' captured faces in real time with the ritual expressions of Kathakali and Theyyam performers, turning the apparatus of biometric capture into a vessel for endangered embodied heritage.

entries.title: Mushroom Clouds
entries.move: Builds a hand-made training dataset from 38 mushroom species found on Lantau Island, feeds it to a custom AI model, and exhibits the model's speculative new fungi beside a living terrarium — a small, sourced dataset set against LLM-scale data hunger.

entries.title: Not the Only One (N'TOO)
entries.move: Trains a sculptural voice-AI oracle exclusively on oral histories from three generations of the artist's own Black family, refusing commercial datasets she considers irreparably biased — the AI's glitches and refusals become deliberate pedagogy about data sovereignty rather than bugs to be fixed.

entries.title: Once Upon A Garden (Once Upon a Flower series)
entries.move: Builds her own GAN training sets from photographed Senegalese flowers and scanned national-archive material — rejecting biased large Western models — to speculatively generate flora that global warming and colonial archival gaps have already erased or never recorded.

entries.title: Patchwork Girl
entries.move: A lecture performance built around an AI-generated avatar assembled from real online-harassment victims' testimonies, confronting audiences with synthesized, composite harm.

entries.title: Pollinator Pathmaker
entries.move: Encodes 'empathy for other species' as a literal algorithmic design parameter: a custom generative tool composes real, physically-planted gardens optimized for maximum pollinator-species diversity across a season, rather than for human visual preference - living, growing plants as the algorithm's actual output.

entries.title: She Who Sees the Unknown
entries.move: 3D-scans and 3D-prints erased or demonized female/queer jinn figures from Middle Eastern mythology, pairing physical sculptures with an open digital archive and storytelling practice she names 'Re-Figuring' — coining and theorizing 'digital colonialism' as a critical framework for whose myths and data get to persist.

entries.title: Source.Plus / PD12M
entries.artist: Spawning (Mat Dryhurst, Holly Herndon, Jordan Meyer)
entries.move: Builds the rights-clear alternative to indiscriminate scraping: public-domain/CC0 images run through nudity, gore and PII classifiers and auto-recaptioned into PD12M, a 12.4-million-pair dataset — provenance-as-infrastructure, don't just flag stolen data, manufacture the clean substitute at training scale.

entries.title: Starmirror
entries.artist: Holly Herndon & Mat Dryhurst, with Sub
entries.move: Trains a voice-cloning model on amateur choirs singing a commissioned songbook rooted in local traditions, turning audiences into willing, credited data-donors — a consensual, opt-in counter-model to nonconsensual voice-cloning.

entries.title: Swell of spæc(i)es
entries.move: Invites visitors to feed AI training sets beyond the Western canon — 3D-scanned West African deity statues, plankton, archival photographs — turning the gallery into a live intervention on whose data trains the machine.

entries.title: Synthetic Memories
entries.move: Reconstructs fading or traumatic personal memories of elderly, dementia-affected, migrant and marginalized people into printed images via generative AI refined through live interviewee feedback loops.

entries.title: The Call
entries.move: Recorded 15 UK community choirs under a purpose-written songbook/recording protocol, then placed the resulting voice dataset under a 'Data Trust' governance experiment (a Trusted Data Intermediary distributing power between contributors and model-users) before using it to train the choral AI models that fill the chapel-like installation — consent becomes both method and subject, not backstory.

entries.title: The Finesse
entries.artist: Christopher Kulendran Thomas, with Annika Kuhlmann
entries.move: An AI continuously scrapes social media and re-edits the film live, weaving a Kardashian-like deepfake avatar into the defeated Tamil liberation movement's history — post-truth authorship as a never-repeating live installation.

entries.title: The Island
entries.move: Stages an actor playing Flash Gordon 'appearing' on the real Croatian island of Korčula to save the world, threading documentary and fiction through sculptural projection-spheres — using 'junk time' vs. 'deep time' to interrogate what counts as real, staged, or generated footage in a media environment already saturated with synthetic images.

entries.title: The Next Biennial Should Be Curated by a Machine
entries.move: An AI trained on real Biennial and Whitney archives endlessly hallucinates fake artist biographies and press releases, exposing algorithmic curation's absurdity by actually letting a machine attempt it, live, forever.

entries.title: The Sleight of the Machine
entries.move: An AI video model is cast as a stage magician performing sleight-of-hand; rather than concealing the model's characteristic failures (hands multiplying, morphing, defying physics), the film keeps every glitch on screen as the actual 'trick' — generative failure turned into the evidentiary content.

entries.title: V3: Model Collapse
entries.move: Third chapter of a four-part project in which each exhibition's own photographs and collages are fed back as training data for the next - literalizes AI model collapse as a visible, physically-installed material process, and draws an explicit parallel between data mining and geological mining extraction.

entries.title: Venenosas, Nocivas e Suspeitas
entries.move: Three years of AI-generated fictional plants and portraits of erased women botanists expose the sexism and colonialism embedded in plant nomenclature; asked to depict aging women accurately, the AI systems balked at rendering wrinkles — their bias becoming part of the evidence on display.

entries.title: xhairymutantx
entries.move: Trains a text-to-image model on costumed, deliberately distorted images of Herndon's own body, so anyone prompting 'Holly Herndon' generates the artist's consented counter-likeness instead of an unauthorized deepfake — a first-person reclaiming of training-data consent.

entries.title: 6,500 Alphabets Make a Map
entries.move: Large-scale dome installation built from 6,500 digitized African pictographs, syllabaries and ideographs (extending the artist's 2019–2023 'Ancestral Algorithm' project) that reframes 'algorithm' as 'algo + rhythm', proposing indigenous knowledge systems as an alternative computational epistemics rather than an ornament to it.

entries.title: A Nation Is a Massacre
entries.move: A large-format text installation that lists/recites five centuries of massacres, missing and murdered Indigenous people, and environmental-racism incidents as a confrontational, register-like data litany covering a gallery floor and walls.

entries.title: Ambiogenesis
entries.move: AI-voiced aquatic organisms narrate a post-human ecosystem with a 'radically different understanding of life and temporality,' using generative voice synthesis to give speculative, non-human timescales a first-person register.

entries.title: Arachnid Orchestra. Jam Sessions
entries.move: Uses piezo pickups and laser Doppler vibrometers to capture real spider-web vibrations, then invites human musicians into live 'jam sessions' improvising alongside the arachnids' actual communication signals - an interspecies sonification instrument built from real vibrational data, not a metaphor for one.

entries.title: Balot NFT / White Cube Lusanga
entries.artist: CATPC (Congolese Plantation Workers Art League) with Human Activities / Renzo Martens
entries.move: Congolese ex-plantation workers mint NFTs of a contested 1931 anti-colonial sculpture ("Balot") held by a Virginia museum, using the sale proceeds to literally buy back plantation land — turning blockchain provenance into a restitution and land-reclamation instrument instead of a speculative art-market gimmick.

entries.title: Barbed Wire Village
entries.artist: Chao Tayiana Maina / Museum of British Colonialism
entries.move: 3D-reconstructs suppressed British 'villagisation' and Mau Mau detention camps from archival and survivor data, rebuilding a physical Nairobi exhibition around a digitally modeled colonial crime scene that Kenya's post-independence archive had erased.

entries.title: Breathing with the Forest
entries.move: Builds an architectural-scale, 3-channel immersive visualization around real carbon, water and mycorrhizal-network data drawn from a single Capinuri tree in the Colombian Amazon, making invisible more-than-human ecological reciprocity perceptible - though its sublime, cinematic staging leans closer to spectacle than to a data-justice argument.

entries.title: Conversations with Bina48
entries.move: Documents a years-long, ongoing videotaped dialogue between the artist and Bina48 — a social robot modeled on a Black woman but never programmed with Black history or identity — exposing the racial blind spots baked into 'universal' AI personhood.

entries.title: Create Your Kampala
entries.move: Surveys 1,000 Kampala residents on failing public services (roads, water, waste, schools), then feeds that citizen dataset back into the city as public wall murals — a data report that returns as something walkable and communal instead of a locked PDF.

entries.title: Cybernetics, or Ghosts?
entries.artist: Michael Salu (editor) & James Ginzburg (music), with 15 international writers
entries.move: Fifteen writers respond in fiction to Italo Calvino's 1967 essay on cybernetics and myth, paired with a companion album, using the generative-AI moment as a mirror held up to older mythic and oral world-building traditions.

entries.title: Data Justice Program & Digital Stewards
entries.year: 2012–ongoing (Digital Stewards from 2012; Data Justice Program from 2016)
entries.move: Trains neighborhood residents as 'Digital Stewards' who physically build community-owned mesh Wi-Fi networks in Detroit neighborhoods, then extends that same infrastructural-sovereignty logic to the city's Open Data portal — resisting extraction by building parallel, community-held technical infrastructure rather than only critiquing the existing one.

entries.title: Estados de Alerta (States of Alert)
entries.move: Three reactive robotic creatures — modeled on latex skin, goat, and cowhide morphologies — read a visitor's approach as threat and answer with self-preservation: sinuous skin tremors, a puff of charcoal dust, deployed steel spikes. The 'Other as threat to private property' is staged as animal instinct rather than human ideology.

entries.title: Feedback VR, un musical antifuturista
entries.move: Peru's hi5-era 'sYmB0l$' internet slang is fused with Andean ritual sites inside a VR musical, reclaiming a decolonized digital vernacular instead of accepting a Silicon-Valley default aesthetic for what 'the future' of the internet is supposed to look like.

entries.title: Forest Art Intelligence (FAI) / Analog Intelligence
entries.move: Sensor-laced, 'lively materials' installations built directly into a regenerating forest ecosystem, treating the site's own ecological data as a co-author of the artwork rather than as a subject observed from outside.

entries.title: Girjegumpi: The Sámi Architecture Library
entries.move: A nomadic, growing archive of 500+ books, artworks and objects on Sámi architecture and decoloniality, built as literal reindeer-herder-cabin infrastructure (and mirrored online as 'The Virtual Girjegumpi') rather than a representation of a library.

entries.title: Give It Back
entries.artist: New Red Order (Jackson Polys, Adam Khalil, Zack Khalil)
entries.move: Deadpan 'public secret society' videos and installations that document real, verifiable instances of land or money actually being returned to Indigenous nations, packaged as satirical settler-recruitment propaganda.

entries.title: Indigenous Protocol and Artificial Intelligence Position Paper
entries.artist: Jason Edward Lewis et al. (Indigenous Protocol and AI Working Group)
entries.move: Convenes Indigenous artists, scholars and technologists to draft founding ethical guidelines asking what AI would look like if it emerged from Indigenous rather than Western epistemologies — the canon document that seeded the later Abundant Intelligences research program.

entries.title: Indigenous Protocols for AI — Gallery 3
entries.artist: Angie Abdilla / Old Ways, New (with Jason Edward Lewis, Oiwi Parker Jones)
entries.move: Develops Indigenous-authored governance protocols ('Country Centred Design') for AI systems through cross-continental workshops (Aotearoa, Australia, North America, Pacific), presented as a public gallery of cultural output rather than a conventional single artwork — positioning First Nations peoples as authors of AI ethics, not subjects of it.

entries.title: Lukautim Solwara (look out for the ocean) / Expanses
entries.move: Performance-video works that re-embed queer, Indigenous Pacific (Sāmoan) bodies into colonial ocean and climate-change narratives, arguing that decolonising climate discourse itself is part of the artwork.

entries.title: Mapu Kufüll (Land Seafood)
entries.move: Uses video-game-style 3D animation to follow a child gathering wild mushrooms under a grandmother's guidance, reclaiming fungi (mapu kufüll) — a food source that helped Mapuche communities survive displacement during the Occupation of Araucanía — as more-than-human ally and symbol of resistance, told through Indigenous rather than Western bio-art framing.

entries.title: Masakhane
entries.move: A distributed, no-prerequisite community ('we build together' in isiZulu) crowdsources open datasets, translation and speech models for African languages historically excluded from big tech's language models — treating linguistic decolonization as ongoing collective infrastructure-building rather than a single authored work.

entries.title: Matrix Vegetal
entries.move: A video installation braids Peruvian plant-healing practices together with 'quantum-inspired' technology, treating indeterminacy and non-Western epistemics of plant communication as equally valid registers of knowledge alongside computation.

entries.title: Meditation on Country
entries.artist: Angie Abdilla, with Ghillar Michael Anderson, Brian Schmidt and Katie Noon
entries.move: An immersive film installation uses machine learning to stage Aboriginal ancestral deep-time knowledge and Western astrophysics side by side under a simulated sky — refusing to let AI default to a single, Western epistemology of the cosmos.

entries.title: MEMORY (Drawing Operations Unit: Generation 2 / D.O.U.G._2)
entries.move: Performs live collaborative drawing alongside a robotic arm driven by a recurrent neural network trained on two decades of her own gestures; the V&A later acquires the trained model itself — sealed in a slowly degrading 3D-printed resin case — the first AI model collected as an artwork by a major museum, staging human/machine co-authorship as more-than-human kinship rather than tool-use.

entries.title: Myconnect
entries.artist: Saša Spačal, Mirjan Švagelj, Anil Podgornik
entries.year: 2013 (Honorary Mention, Prix Ars Electronica 2015; Prix Cube 2016 nominee)
entries.move: A participant's heartbeat is converted to an electrical signal and fed live into oyster/shiitake mycelium cultures in petri dishes; the mycelium's bioelectric resistance response is captured and converted back into vibration, sound and light for the participant - a literal two-way 'mycosynapse' between human vital signs and a living fungal network, questioning the anthropocentric division of nature-human-technology.

entries.title: Mythmachine
entries.move: An AI-driven virtual biome of post-human creatures listens to and choreographs itself from ambient audio feedback captured live in the gallery, proposing folklore-derived 'other' intelligences as an alternative to extractive machine learning.

entries.title: Nepenthe (Summer Palace Ruins Edition)
entries.move: Digitally rebuilds the looted, burned ruins of the Yuanmingyuan Summer Palace as a walkable open-world game space, turning a colonial wound into explorable virtual terrain and raising the question of virtual restitution.

entries.title: netart_latino database
entries.move: A hand-coded, ASCII-mapped database indexes Latin American net artists by national domain (.mx, .ve, .uy...) instead of Northern-institution categories — an inverted cartography that makes the region a creative center rather than a periphery importing art from elsewhere.

entries.title: Night Fishing with Ancestors
entries.move: An Indigenous-run collective of roughly 30 Belyuen community members re-stages 18th-century Macassan–Aboriginal trade history using iPhone-shot 'improvisational realism,' layering and superimposing footage to collapse colonial linear time into simultaneous ancestral and contemporary registers.

entries.title: No conciliation is possible (working diagram)
entries.move: A site-specific wall-diagram installation (map-like drawings, objects, annotations) that treats decolonization as unfinished, still-computing political data rather than a settled historical fact — the diagram-as-system is the artwork, not a single image.

entries.title: Nosukaay
entries.move: A hand-woven West African (Manjak) loincloth functions as a literal keyboard/interface, arguing that weaving and computing share a common ancestral logic — an alternative, non-Western origin story for the machine.

entries.title: Our Data Bodies / Digital Defense Playbook
entries.artist: Our Data Bodies Project (Detroit Community Technology Project, Stop LAPD Spying Coalition, Center for Community Transitions)
entries.move: Runs two years of workshops in Detroit, Charlotte and LA neighborhoods so residents can map how re-entry, housing and welfare data systems police them, then distills the findings into a free community 'Digital Defense Playbook' of counter-surveillance tools instead of an academic report.

entries.title: overturns
entries.move: Reworks Sylvia Wynter's call to overturn Western 'genres of the human' into a suite of diagrams, models and sculptural systems mapping planetary racial capital against co-existing Black and Indigenous cosmologies — treating decolonization as a systems/data problem, not a site-specific one.

entries.title: Paradise Camp
entries.move: Restages Gauguin's Sāmoa-derived colonial-ethnographic paintings as tableau photographs with a Fa'afafine cast, building a counter-archive ('Vārchive') that exposes the source images while entangling colonisation, gender and climate catastrophe.

entries.title: Phyto-Travellers
entries.move: A living garden of colonial-era "neophyte" plants is grown on freight pallets inside a 2:3-scale reconstruction of Columbus's ship the Niña, with the plants' original indigenous names inscribed on the glass façade — a literal, growing archive of botanical colonialism rather than a data visualization of it.

entries.title: PL'AI
entries.move: An AI-controlled robot 'plays' with live cucumber plants in a terrarium via Lidar scanning and colored-ball placement, forcing a literal, physical protocol of interspecies communication between machine intelligence and plant behavior rather than a metaphorical one.

entries.title: Primate Visions: Macaque Macabre
entries.move: Turns Sulawesi crested macaques — framed by colonial primatology as lesser life — into protagonists of a camp horror-theatre cosmology drawn from Minahasan belief, granting agency to more-than-human entities against anthropocentric state modernity.

entries.title: Pȟehíŋ kiŋ líla akhíšoke (Her hair was heavy)
entries.move: Performs wearing a braided-hair interface woven with sensors and machine learning that 'listens without ears,' translating touch and movement into light, sound and AI-generated text — staging the technology as a spirit-greeting device within Lakȟóta protocol rather than a neutral tool.

entries.title: Repatriate (and broader climate-performance practice)
entries.move: The Tongan-Australian artist's own body performs an endurance ritual — dancing a Tongan liturgical choreography inside a Perspex tank slowly filled by fire hydrants over 90 minutes — as a direct physical proxy for Pacific sea-level-rise data.

entries.title: Repellent Fence
entries.move: Floats 26 ten-foot 'scare-eye' balloons, decorated with Indigenous medicine colors, in a two-mile line straddling the US/Mexico border — a temporary, four-day land-art 'suture' re-joining Indigenous land that a colonial border fence had divided.

entries.title: SummitShare — Open Digital Infrastructure for Shared Histories (Cultural Heritage)
entries.artist: SummitShare / Shared Histories Team (Mulenga Kapwepwe, Thomas Gondwe, Nhyira Amofa-Sekyi, Mario Jere)
entries.move: A blockchain-based open-access virtual museum performing 'metadata healing' on colonial-era Zambian artifacts, centering indigenous women custodians and routing financial support back to heritage communities.

entries.title: Takapau
entries.artist: Mataaho Collective (Erena Baker, Sarah Hudson, Bridget Reweti, Terri Te Tau)
entries.move: Monumental woven/lashed hi-vis tie-down installation that scales a domestic, matrilineal Māori fibre-craft practice — mat-weaving used in childbirth ceremony — up to architectural size, forming the Arsenale's entry passage.

entries.title: The Kris Project (I–III)
entries.move: Splices found footage from 1950s–60s Cathay-Keris Malayan cinema with wartime documentary material through an invented fictional filmmaker persona, collapsing fact and propaganda to expose whose version of Malayan history counts as 'archival record.'

entries.title: The Open Boat
entries.move: A sound/performance piece built from postcolonial theory and the non-linear, cyclical temporalities of oceanic space, staging Black Atlantic migration and diaspora as a counter-epistemology to Western linear data and archival logic.

entries.title: The Planetary Compendium
entries.move: A living, continuously evolving digital atlas of essays and case studies mapping planetary-governance frameworks, built as a scalable educational tool rather than a fixed artwork.

entries.title: The REDress Project
entries.move: Empty red dresses (400+, many donated by families) hung in public sites across North America to make the uncounted statistical gap of missing and murdered Indigenous women viscerally, spatially present as absence.

entries.title: Three Experiments in Plant Intercognition
entries.move: Stages literal cognitive-communication experiments between artist and germinating plants (extending her 'Skotopoiesis' bio-semiotic method), treating a plant's measurable response to light and stimuli as a form of intelligence to test the human-drawn boundaries of cognition.

entries.title: Transfiguraciones
entries.move: A GAN trained on digitized datasets of Prehispanic Mesoamerican masks is played live like an instrument, its outputs morphing in real time under the performers' control — the neural network treated as a possessed object to be exorcised/decolonized rather than a neutral generative tool.

entries.title: Uncharted
entries.move: 6,500 characters collected from African and diasporic writing systems are rendered as an AI-driven data sculpture that a dancer must physically interpret in real time — an endangered-language archive made legible only through embodied performance, not a screen or a search bar.

entries.title: Yanmeeyarr
entries.move: Ochre body-marking patterns used in Gunditjmara ceremony, translated into a light-and-shadow installation across the museum's ceiling, framing the threshold visitors cross into and out of a history of the moving image.

entries.title: AI, Ain't I a Woman?
entries.move: A spoken-word video poem restages Sojourner Truth's 1851 question through five commercial facial-analysis APIs (Microsoft, IBM, Amazon, Face++, Google) misgendering Oprah, Serena Williams, Michelle Obama and Shirley Chisholm on screen — turns benchmark error rates into a recited indictment.

entries.title: Algorithmic Justice League
entries.move: Institutionalizes 'the coded gaze' as a named, citable object of critique — fuses art, research and policy testimony into a standing instrument that keeps auditing deployed AI systems rather than resting on a single artwork.

entries.title: Coded Bias
entries.artist: Shalini Kantayya (director), featuring Joy Buolamwini, Cathy O'Neil, Zeynep Tufekci, Safiya Noble, Deborah Raji
entries.move: Documents the Gender Shades audit escalating into congressional testimony and municipal facial-recognition bans, narrativizing an algorithmic accuracy study as a feminist accountability thriller.

entries.title: Data Feminism
entries.move: Reframes data science through intersectional feminist theory, arguing that counting and classification themselves encode power — turns 'whose voice is missing from the data' into a repeatable analytic method rather than a moral aside.

entries.title: Dear Data
entries.move: Two designers mail each other one hand-drawn postcard a week for a year, each encoding a mundane personal metric (complaints, doors touched, laughter) — asserts 'data humanism': the antidote to extractive big data is slow, subjective, handmade small data shared as intimacy.

entries.title: Decoding Bias
entries.move: Eight hyper-realistic AI avatars are staged in a self-run group-therapy circle to 'purge' their own biased training data and toxic code — algorithmic bias literalized as a confession the machines are made to perform in front of a live audience.

entries.title: Feminist Data Set
entries.move: Interrogates every stage of a machine-learning pipeline — collection, labeling, training, algorithm choice, chatbot design — through participatory feminist workshops, treating deliberately slow, intentional data-gathering itself as an act of protest against extractive data culture.

entries.title: Gender Shades
entries.move: Builds an intersectional benchmark (Pilot Parliaments Benchmark, 1,270 faces) to show commercial gender-classifiers erring up to 34.7% on darker-skinned women versus 0.8% on lighter-skinned men — an academic audit engineered as public evidence, which pushed IBM to end facial-recognition sales.

entries.title: Harvesting Climate Action
entries.move: Combines digital sensing tools with community culinary-identity workshops in a three-tiered (individual/group/district) structure to build climate-data awareness from the ground up.

entries.title: Here the River Lies
entries.move: Crowdsources 1,500+ oral micro-histories of a vanished river onto a hand-drawn map and deliberately refuses to distinguish verified memory from invented story, indexing both into the same archive as a challenge to the evidentiary claims of official heritage data.

entries.title: Minotauros (Minotaurs)
entries.move: An 8-bit-aesthetic LED labyrinth animates Mexico City's informal-economy occupation rate — rendering, in low-resolution video-game imagery, the workers who accumulate no data trail toward a pension: missing data made visibly to move.

entries.title: Missing Datasets (list/essay)
entries.move: An open, continually-added public list plus essay cataloguing real-world datasets that go uncollected, giving the physical Library's concept a living, crowd-legible digital counterpart.

entries.title: Shifting Sands: A Battle Song
entries.move: Gathers texts, drawings, and voice recordings from over 1,000 Saudi women across nationwide workshops into a single immersive multimedia installation, converting collected first-person testimony into a national-pavilion-scale statistical portrait of women's status.

entries.title: Sobrevivientes
entries.artist: Datasketch (with Sandra Suárez / QueremosDatos.co, Data Against Feminicide network)
entries.move: Denied complete femicide records through freedom-of-information requests, the team built its own database from news reports and survivor testimony, then translated the gaps into embroidery, illustration, digital maps, and a public-space intervention — data activism that makes the state's non-counting visible.

entries.title: Stealth Care: Wellness from the Algorithm
entries.move: The artist's own chronically-ill, 'non-normative' muscle data, captured via a wearable EMG device over six months of research with Ars Electronica x IT:U, is fed into ML models built for wellness/health platforms — exposing whose bodies the quantified-self industry was never built to include.

entries.title: The Library of Missing Datasets
entries.move: A literal filing cabinet of empty, labeled folders — each naming a dataset that societies choose not to collect (e.g. undocumented migrants incarcerated in the US) — makes structural absence itself the exhibit.

entries.title: The Library of Missing Datasets (v2.0)
entries.move: Fills steel filing cabinets with empty folders labeled by the names of datasets that structurally do not exist ('People excluded from housing due to criminal records', 'Uncounted deaths tied to Hurricane Maria') — making data's absence itself the exhibit, by a Nigerian-American artist working at the intersection of data collection and racial/social omission.

entries.title: Vigil
entries.move: A durational street performance — scrubbing the pavement, yelling the first names of real missing women written on her arms, then nailing a red dress to a pole until it tears — marking the unresolved case count of over 65 missing Downtown Eastside women.

entries.title: The Feral: Epoch 1
entries.move: First chapter of a planned 1,000-year, 32-generation project in which successive artists 'feed' one AI so it can eventually make a film witnessing humanity's end — a deliberately glacial experiment in what a machine 'learns' across centuries rather than scraped-in-seconds data.

entries.title: Thousand Lives (BOB lineage)

entries.title: ASSEMBLY
entries.move: Traces the Michela stenographic keyboard used for real Italian and Australian parliamentary record-keeping, following its data as it is translated across written word, code, music and choreography, filmed inside actual Senate chambers.

entries.title: Climate temperature-anomaly sonification
entries.move: Converts global land-based temperature anomalies since 1880 (Berkeley Earth dataset) into one musical note per year against a 1950-1980 baseline, making 150 years of warming audible as an accelerating, increasingly dissonant climb rather than a chart.

entries.title: data-verse (trilogy)

entries.title: DATALAND
entries.artist: Refik Anadol Studio (Refik Anadol & Efsun Erkılıç)

entries.title: teamLab Borderless
entries.move: Included deliberately as the spectacle-pole counterweight: real-time motion-tracking and projection-mapped generative visuals produce pure immersive wonder with no explicit interrogation of data, AI, or power — the mirror image of every investigation-pole work in this set.

entries.title: The Street is Watching You (Face the Vitrine)
entries.move: Projects giant tracking eyes onto a downtown Cairo storefront so passersby physically feel themselves being watched in real time — literalizing street harassment and the CCTV/state gaze as a shared bodily experience instead of an abstract policy debate.

entries.title: Unsupervised
entries.move: Runs a generative model over 138,151 digitized works from MoMA's own collection and streams the output as a continuously mutating real-time 'hallucination' on a 24×24-ft media wall — no argument, no disclosed critique of the compute/energy behind it; over 3 million visitors, pure data-sublime as the point.

entries.move: Diary of happiness was a large-scale installation created by Jean-Michel Othoniel for his solo show in Miami in 2008.
